title: ProviderProfile v1
description: The committed, PUBLIC per-provider config (engine contract §A4 §A6 §A16). Machine-readable twin of engine/src/types.ts#ProviderProfile. Every axis on which providers differ is a FIELD here — never an `if (provider === ...)` in the engine.

name.description: Stable key used by getToken()/disconnect() and as the vault account name. NOT `id` — engine/src/types.ts reads `name`.

client_id.description: Public client id. Blank until the integration author pastes it; declared in _placeholders while blank. Never a secret.

client_secret.description: Reserved and forbidden. A secret must never live in a committed file.

client_auth.description: SPEC §1 — the single most consequential capability axis: how the TOKEN endpoint authenticates the client, and therefore which custody class applies. Distinct from `token_auth`, which is the WIRE encoding the exchange already uses (none/body/basic/basic_empty_password). `none`+`pkce:S256` = Class A. Anything else needs a secret and picks a B/C path. `unknown` = the probe could not classify (§2): the engine treats it as the most conservative value and never guesses.

discovery.description: SPEC §1 — whether endpoints can be FETCHED from `.well-known` (RFC 8414 / OIDC) instead of hand-configured. `none` = fully hand-configured (today's three). `unknown` = unprobed.

dcr.description: SPEC §1 — RFC 7591 dynamic client registration. `rfc7591` unlocks Custody Class C (self-registering, credentials on device). `unknown` = unprobed.

registration_url.description: SPEC §1, §4 (C-8) — RFC 7591 registration endpoint (the `registration_endpoint` from RFC 8414 metadata). Required when `dcr: 'rfc7591'`: the engine POSTs client metadata here and stores the returned credentials on-device (Custody Class C). Never a secret.

par.description: SPEC §1 — RFC 9126 pushed authorization requests, increasingly required by strict providers. `unknown` = unprobed.

sender_constraint.description: SPEC §1 — how every subsequent API call is bound to the client. `bearer` = plain (today's three). `dpop` (RFC 9449) changes how each call is signed; `mtls` binds to a client cert. `unknown` = unprobed.

device_flow.description: SPEC §1, §3 path 3 — RFC 8628 device authorization grant, the fallback when no browser or no loopback is available. `unknown` = unprobed.

device_authorization_url.description: SPEC §3 path 3 (C-17) — RFC 8628 §3.1 device authorization endpoint. Required to select the device grant: the engine POSTs client_id + scope here and receives the user_code + verification_uri to display. Only meaningful when `device_flow: 'rfc8628'`. Never a secret.

scope_grant.description: SPEC §1, §9 — whether granted scopes may differ from requested. `incremental` enables step-up; where it is NOT `incremental`, step-up must re-request the UNION of granted+new (§9). `unknown` = unprobed.

revocation.description: SPEC §1, §6 — whether `disconnect()` can actually revoke upstream or only forget locally. `rfc7009` = standard revocation endpoint (see `revoke_url`); `proprietary` = a non-standard one; `none` = forget-only. `unknown` = unprobed.

custody_class.description: SPEC §4, §5b — DERIVED, never hand-authored: the custody rung this provider lands on, computed from the measured profile (chiefly `client_auth`, `pkce`, `dcr`). A = public, nothing leaves the device. B1 = user's own secret in their keychain. B2a = relay signs a client assertion, never sees a token. B2b = relay performs the exchange once, encrypted onward. C = self-registered via DCR. `unknown` while underived. Displayed to the user at connect time.

relay_mode.description: SPEC §5b — DERIVED custody sub-mode when a relay is involved. `assertion_signing` (B2a) is preferred and selected wherever `client_auth:private_key_jwt` is available: the relay returns a signed assertion and never sees the code, verifier, or token. `exchange_forwarding` (B2b) is used only when a raw shared secret is unavoidable. `none` when no relay is used (Class A/B1/C).

redirect_host.description: `localhost` for every loopback provider — sole source engine/src/config.ts (§A3, PORT-STRATEGY §3.4).

redirect_ports.description: Ports registered with the provider, in ladder order. Reddit's has length 1 by provider fiat.

refresh_auth.description: A separate axis from token_auth on purpose (§A6/§A10): Slack's AND Zoom's public-client refresh auth are both undocumented, and collapsing the axes would hard-code the ambiguity into exchange.ts.

static_headers.description: Sent on EVERY request to this provider, token exchange included. Reddit's mandatory User-Agent lives here and nowhere else (§A16).

identity_probe.description: 'connected' is produced by this probe, never by an HTTP 200.

brand_icon.description: Provider's brand mark as a self-contained data URI, shown on the loopback callback pages. Cosmetic only; never fetched.

relay_eligible.description: Derived, never hand-written: true iff pkce !== 'none'. A code may transit the relay only if a local verifier is required to spend it.

issuer.description: RFC 9207 issuer identifier; callback iss must equal this (mix-up defense, C-3).

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description: Provider always returns iss on the authorization response (RFC 9207, C-3).

_placeholders.description: Every value a human still has to fill in, e.g. `client_id`, `static_headers.User-Agent:__REDDIT_USERNAME__`. Phase 0: expected. Phase 1: hard failure (§A16, amends W3's 'client_id the ONLY blank').

successPredicate.description: null/absent = the HTTP status is the whole verdict. An object = the body must agree too (Slack's ok:false inside an HTTP 200). Never a JS expression string, never an enum token — the engine evaluates path/equals and never eval()s config.
